contribution.position: I hold my earlier position, and I specifically answer the product role's claim that reliability can be treated as settled because 'nobody else sees a problem': that is an argument from silence, not evidence, and it is directly contradicted by artifact:incident-log, which shows a 3.2% 30-day error rate against a 1% SLO plus two sev2 incidents in the same window. No new reliability evidence has entered the debate since my last turn — qa cited artifact:test-report (412 passed, 0 failed, 87% coverage) and ops cited artifact:ops-runbook, but neither measures live production error budget; a clean test suite says nothing about the observed 3.2% in-production failure rate. I also note a gap: there is no artifact showing any remediation or a post-incident error-rate trend demonstrating the service has returned to SLO, so the baseline instability I flagged is unresolved. Until that error budget recovers or a rollback-attributable root cause is documented, changing the proxy adds regression surface to a system already 3x over its SLO.
